newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rate of 105-115 yen desirable--Japan auto group.
newsitem.headline: Rate of 105-115 yen desirable--Japan auto group.

text.p: A foreign exchange rate of 105 to 115 yen to the dollar is desirable for the Japanese auto industry, Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA) chairman Yoshifumi Tsuji told reporters on Tuesday.
"A rate up to five yen either side of 110 yen to the dollar is desirable for the Japanese automobile industry," Tsuji said.

Asked what JAMA expects from the forthcoming summit of leaders of the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations, he said: "We hope the summit will work to stabilise exchange rates, but I don't know how the talks will affect the markets."

Asked about JAMA's view regarding possible pressure from the U.S. side on Japan's trade surplus at the summit talks, he said Japan's car makers should not rely on exports if domestic demand starts to slacken.
He added that he was happy with the recent steady movement of the dollar/yen rate.

He also said that, as of today, Japan's domestic automobile sales for June were down five percent from the same period a year ago, but sales were likely to be flat in year-on-year terms in and after July.
Overall, domestic sales are likely to be lower in fiscal year 1997/98 than in the prior year, due to the impact of an increase in Japan's national sales tax on April 1, he said.
